questions.q: What are the four components of emotional intelligence?
a: Knowing yourself, managing yourself, reading others and handling relationships
Self-esteem, ambition, charisma and public speaking
Empathy, patience, optimism and resilience
Listening, persuasion, negotiation and networking
questions.why: Lesson 1 names four parts: knowing yourself, managing yourself, reading others and handling relationships.

questions.q: What is the emotion versus reason list?
a: Two columns comparing what feelings and logic urge
A list of reasons to avoid emotional conversations
A chart ranking emotions from weak to strong
A record of every emotion you felt that day
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests writing what your emotions want in one column and what logical reasoning says in another, then comparing them.

questions.q: Why should your body language match your words?
a: Mixed signals make your message seem insincere
Matching gestures make you speak more quickly
Body language matters only in job interviews
Words are remembered longer than expressions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says rushing through thanks without smiling sends mixed signals, so the message stops sounding sincere.

questions.q: Why does the book recommend asking close people for feedback?
a: It shows what you do well and what to improve
It proves to them that you value their opinions
It gives you material for future conversations
It prevents them from criticizing you behind your back
questions.why: Lesson 3 says feedback is the only way to learn what you are doing right and wrong, though it can feel like criticism.

questions.q: How can friends and family support self-management?
a: Knowing your goals keeps you accountable to them
They can make decisions for you when you are stressed
They can shield you from difficult situations
They can remind you to suppress your emotions
questions.why: Lesson 2 says telling family and friends your goals gives you accountability, which is a strong source of motivation.
